clue.text: Folio — loose leaves from it make cloth

parts.note: lax means loose or slack

explanation.surface: A loose-leaf folio is being turned into fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like the folio's pages; the definition loosely describes the plant whose fibres are woven into linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is woven from fibres of this plant, so cloth is made from it.

clue.text: Emergency flight perhaps liberates peninsula flanking island

indicators.note: flanking means on either side of, so the liberates word goes round the island letter

parts.note: frees means liberates
a cape is a headland or peninsula

explanation.surface: An escape route frees a peninsula hemmed round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanking' signals the island letter is surrounded. 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not an escape by air.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire escape is an emergency staircase, a flight of steps for leaving a burning building.

clue.text: Section of supermarket with intricate design clipped at the edges

indicators.note: clipped at the edges means trimmed of its first and last letters

parts.note: paisley is an intricate swirling fabric pattern

explanation.surface: A supermarket section is decorated with an intricate pattern trimmed round the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped at the edges' drops P and Y from PAISLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermarket shelves are arranged along aisles, the walkways between them.

clue.text: Laic, i.e. just out of priestly order?

indicators.note: out here means put out of place, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A layman wonders whether he has just been thrown out of a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals that LAIC, IE and JUST are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the Society of Jesus, a priestly order.

clue.text: Extraordinary ability with English was sufficient for contrived language

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is an extraordinary ability
ran to means stretched to or was enough for

explanation.surface: Remarkable English skills were enough for an invented tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial language created by Zamenhof, hence contrived.

clue.text: Perhaps scorer's more uplifted about New Zealand Open?

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned word goes round New Zealand
uplifted in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: più is Italian for more, used as a musical direction by a composer, one who writes a score

explanation.surface: A goal-scorer celebrates higher still over the New Zealand Open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifted' turns the Italian word backwards and 'about' wraps it round. The scorer is a composer writing a score, not a goal-scorer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unzip a bag or file is to open it.

clue.text: Flat prohibition on reduced fat

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, a prohibition

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the fat word goes

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A ban on low-fat food leaves things flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts LARD to LAR; 'on' puts TABU above it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabular means flat and broad, like a table top.

clue.text: Vicar put out with Hair's cacophony

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A vicar is put out by the noise from the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges VICAR and HAIR. A charivari is a mock serenade of banging pans.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a discordant din, a cacophony of noise.

clue.text: Like healthy plants, one wants a lot to drink

definitions.text: one wants a lot to drink

explanation.definitionFit: Lush means luxuriant in growth, and as a noun it means a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Small winger in school is a pain for the side

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A small bird in a school proves a nuisance to the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' suggests a team, but it is the side of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side, often from running.

clue.text: Pink stone met the demands of attack from the rear

parts.note: to rise to a challenge is to meet its demands

indicators.note: read from the rear, so the word for attack runs backwards

parts.note: zap means attack or strike

explanation.surface: A pink stone answers the call of an assault from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the rear' turns the attack word backwards. 'Pink stone' could suggest a building stone, but it is a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose topaz is a pink-tinted variety of the gemstone topaz.

clue.text: Banks primarily over burn?

indicators.note: primarily means first, so just the opening letter of Banks
over signals turning the word for burn backwards

parts.note: to sear is to burn

explanation.surface: Mostly banks rise above a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the burn word backwards. A burn is also a Scottish stream, and these Scottish hillsides overlook it, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish braes are hillsides or banks, typically sloping down to a burn or stream.

clue.text: Flat race wanting a versatile horse

parts.note: even means flat or level

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the a is dropped from the word for race

parts.note: to tear is to race or rush

explanation.surface: A flat race lacks a horse with all-round skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting a' removes A from TEAR, leaving TER. 'Flat race' suggests a horse race on the flat.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer competes in eventing, which combines dressage, cross-country and showjumping, so needs versatility.

clue.text: Greek character left a German board in disorder

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A Greek letter left by a German board lies scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile in is to board a vehicle in a disorderly crush of people.

clue.text: Be quick to fill half of sump for freedom from contamination

indicators.note: to fill means going inside, so the be quick word sits within the other
half of keeps only the first half of the word for sump

parts.note: a cesspool is a sump for waste
to hasten is to be quick

explanation.surface: Hurrying to fill a half-empty sump keeps it clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the first four letters of the sump word, and 'to fill' puts the be-quick word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasteness is purity, the state of being free from moral contamination.

clue.text: Brewed herb tea's become popular to start to recover from exercise

indicators.note: to start places the popularity phrase at the front of the answer

parts.note: to catch on is to become popular

indicators.note: brewed means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the s of tea's is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: A brewed herbal tea has become fashionable as a post-workout pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' rearranges HERB TEAS into ESBREATH; 'to start' puts CATCH ON first.
explanation.definitionFit: After exercise one pauses to recover normal breathing, which is the idiom here.

clue.text: Most of dull Lenten cooking was boring

indicators.note: cooking means altering or mixing, so these letters are rearranged
most of means drop the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Most dull Lenten cooking was tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts DULL to DUL, then 'cooking' rearranges DUL and LENTEN. 'boring' means drilling, not dull.
explanation.definitionFit: To tunnel is to bore through earth, so tunnelled means was boring.

clue.text: Singular American movie, one being shown as Hitchcock classic

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a movie
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means being shown, as a film is on

explanation.surface: A one-off American film is screened as a Hitchcock classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion is a 1941 Alfred Hitchcock thriller starring Cary Grant.

clue.text: Long timber upright is framing old location for pictures

parts.note: to pine is to long for
wood is timber
a stud is an upright post in a wall frame

indicators.note: framing means surrounding, so is goes round the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A long upright timber is framing an old site for showing pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' puts O inside IS to give IOS. Pinewood Studios is a major British film studio west of London, so 'pictures' means films, not paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinewood Studios is a famous English film studio where movies, called pictures, are made.

clue.text: I'm sore upset, see, I'm wretched!

annotationWithheld.why: I'm sore upset, see, I'm wretched! (3,2,2): the fodder I'M SORE cannot give WOE IS ME (an R where W and E are needed), and no scan or search gives the printed text
annotationWithheld.clue: I'm sore upset, see, I'm wretched!

clue.text: Raise sympathy with attitude

parts.note: to up a price is to raise it
pity means sympathy

explanation.surface: Show more sympathy, but with some attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity means arrogant or self-important, behaving with attitude.

clue.text: Least abundant four out of five non- Communist countries

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so the numeral for four is removed from five

parts.note: taken as the word itself
IV is four in Roman numerals
the West was the Cold War name for the non-Communist countries

explanation.surface: The fewest countries: four in every five outside the Communist bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four out of five' takes IV from FIVE, leaving FE. 'Four out of five' reads like a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of few means smallest in number, i.e. least abundant.

clue.text: Some ivory whisks utilised selectively to make a flip?

indicators.note: to make a flip means turned over, so the chosen run reads backwards
selectively means only some letters from the run of words are chosen

explanation.surface: Some ivory whisks are used selectively to flip something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'selectively' picks the run SKSUT from 'whisks utilised', and 'to make a flip' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory comes from tusks, so tusks are some ivory.

clue.text: Admission of outmoded person's hopeless situation?

definitions.meaning: someone out of date might confess I am out of fashion, in two words split differently
a deadlock or position with no way forward

explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PASSÉ, the answer is what an outmoded person admits.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a situation where no progress is possible.

clue.text: Thick cushion for nestling

definitions.meaning: a thick stuffed cushion, as on a seat

explanation.definitionFit: A squab is a padded cushion and also a young pigeon still in the nest.

clue.text: Chest rising under old ladies' fingers

indicators.note: under places the chest word below the old letter in this down clue
rising in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an ark is a chest or coffer

explanation.surface: A chest rises beneath the fingers of old ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ARK to KRA, put 'under' O. 'Ladies' fingers' is a name for the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are commonly called ladies' fingers in Britain.

clue.text: Son follows line preserved by family bakers

indicators.note: follows places the son letter after the rest
preserved by means held inside, so the line letter sits within the word for family

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A son carries on a family line of bakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserved by' puts L inside KIN; 'follows' puts S after. Bakers here are ovens, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilns are ovens that bake pottery or bricks, so they are bakers in a cryptic sense.

clue.text: Book writer's benefit entertaining international university

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the benefit word goes round the rest

parts.note: for the sake of means for the benefit of
Intl is a standard abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: An author profits by hosting a global university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts the abbreviations inside the benefit word. 'Book writer' is the author of a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The evangelist traditionally wrote the third gospel and Acts, books of the Bible.

clue.text: Speaking to a theologian about Sunday's first chant

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Sunday

parts.note: to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A divine talks about the hymns sung first thing on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressing someone means speaking to them directly.

clue.text: Bird is shielding front half of beak

indicators.note: shielding means covering, so is surrounds the other piece
only the front half of the word for beak is kept

parts.note: a bird's beak is its bill

explanation.surface: A bird shields the front of its beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front half of' keeps the first two letters of the beak word; 'shielding' puts them inside the clue's own 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill.
